• Sexual Propagation (Seeds): Involves the fusion of male and female gametes. It
  • promotes genetic diversity but may result in offspring different from the parent.

questions.question: List out the different methods of vegetatitive propagation. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Asexual Propagation (Vegetative): Uses vegetative parts like stems, roots, or leaves.
  • o Cuttings: Rooting a piece of the parent plant.
  • o Grafting/Budding: Joining parts from two different plants so they
  • grow as one.
  • o Layering: Inducing roots on a stem while it is still attached to the
  • parent.
  • o Micropropagation: Growing whole plants from cells in a sterile
  • laboratory.

questions.question: List out detached scion method of grafting. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Detached Scion Grafting: A method where the scion is completely separated from
  • the mother plant before being joined to the rootstock. Examples include wedge
  • grafting, tongue grafting, and cleft grafting.

questions.question: How plant propagation helps in disease free plant production? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Disease-Free Plant Production: Propagation helps through meristem
  • culture (which eliminates viruses because the growing tip is often pathogen-free) and
  • by using certified disease-free mother plants or resistant rootstocks.

questions.question: Define line sowing (drilling). / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Line Sowing (Drilling): The process of sowing seeds in continuous lines at a
  • controlled depth and uniform spacing, usually done using a seed drill or by hand in
  • furrows.

questions.question: Write a short note on compound layering. / [CO2] [2x5 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Compound Layering: Also known as serpentine layering. A long branch is
  • alternately covered with soil and left exposed at intervals. Roots form at every buried
  • node, allowing multiple plants to be produced from a single shoot.

questions.question: Describe the different steps involved in seed preparation before sowing. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Seed Preparation
  • Extraction: Removing seeds from the fruit or pod.
  • Drying: Reducing moisture to ensure longevity.
  • Cleaning/Grading: Removing debris and selecting heavy, healthy seeds.
  • Seed Treatment: Using fungicides to prevent disease or techniques like scarification to
  • break dormancy.

questions.question: Write a note on the importance of plant propagation in agriculture. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Importance of plant propagation in agriculture
  • • Ensures Continuous Supply of Planting Material
  • • Helps Maintain Genetic Purity and Uniformity
  • • Enables Improvement of Crop Varieties
  • • Conserves Elite and Rare Germplasm
  • • Facilitates Rapid Multiplication of Plants
  • • Essential for Perennial and Horticultural Crops
  • • Enhances Disease-Free Plant Production
  • • Supports Commercial Agriculture and Nurseries
